newsitem.title: UK: IPE OIL FUTURES EDGE BACK ON US, BUT STILL IN RED.
newsitem.headline: IPE OIL FUTURES EDGE BACK ON US, BUT STILL IN RED.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures cut some of their early losses on Thursday on the back of a stronger than expected NYMEX but with expectations of Iraqi crude hitting the market soon, they continued in the red, traders said.

September Brent was 15 cents down at $19.05 a barrel by 1434 GMT, up from an intra-day low of $18.88 reached a few hours earlier, largely on the Iraqi news. August gas oil, which dipped to as low as $172 a tonne, was $2.25 a tonne down at $173.
"The market is a little stronger now. The NYMEX products are stronger on opening than they were on ACCESS so that's may be why the market is starting to climb," one trader said.

NYMEX's September crude contract was five cents a barrel down at $20.41 after trading up to 24 cents down on the open. Both heating oil and unleaded gasoline futures were also in the red, but stronger than the open.
Traders also said that a force majeure on a number of gasoline cargoes in Venezuela was also giving the market support.

"New York is behaving relatively well so that's helping the market here. Also there the Venezuelan force majeure which I think is giving support to gasoline," a trader said, adding that Brent may climb further.
"The Iraqi news is already in the price and has been mulled over by traders," he added. "I think we may see it (Brent) going higher but not necessarily reaching high reached in the past two days."
Other traders said that the markets were still watching for the final decision on Iraq's crude pricing formula, which the U.N. sanctions committee has until late Friday to vote on.

"The Security Council has until tomorrow to approve it and then it will just be a question of how much oil they (Iraqis) will sell...That question is still on the back of everyone's mind," a trader said.

Traders say Baghdad will have to resume exports at a maximum capacity of 1.8 million barrels per day (bpd) in order to achieve by early September the interim $1 billion target -- or half the total sales allowed under the 180-day oil-for-food deal.
